Hi Rajesh / Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed around encryption and key management: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- PII classification & retention controls: you want per-customer retention windows and the ability to purge data on request.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (ideally TLS 1.3) for all client <> Redwood traffic and mutual TLS for private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 by default; support for Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) so keys never stored in Redwood-managed KMS.
- HSM requirement: Acme compliance may require HSM-backed key storage for some regulated datasets.
- Audit and access logs: detailed audit trail for key usage, API calls, and access to plaintext (if any).

What Redwood can provide (high level):
- Hosted API: envelope encryption with optional CMEK via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault ARNs.
- Private deployment: option to integrate with on-prem or cloud HSMs and a KMS bridge for HSM-backed keys.
- Logs: configurable retention, ability to ship audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket with your encryption settings; sensitive payloads redacted by default.
- Rotation & separation: support for key rotation and key separation (keys scoped per-tenant) so Acme keys do not mix with other customers.

Attachments I've included for initial review: redwood-kms-options.pdf (short overview).

Next steps we agreed on:
1) Dev (copied) will follow up with a technical note on integration patterns (CMEK, HSM, envelope encryption) and sample config.
2) We will send SOC2 summary and redacted report for your compliance team.
3) Schedule a technical deep dive (30–45m) next week with your security team — Rajesh, please suggest times.

If you want, I can also pull together a recommended config for Acme's high-compliance profile to share with your compliance lead.

Thanks,

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks for the great questions — copying Neha for any additional security notes. Below are concise answers and references; attaching a short integration guide and a redacted SOC2 for your compliance review.

1) CMEK / BYOK behavior:
- Hosted: Redwood uses envelope encryption. Data is encrypted with a data key generated by Redwood, the data key is encrypted (envelope) with your CMEK in your KMS (you supply the key ARN). Redwood does NOT persist customer key material in plaintext and does not store your KMS customer key. We only store the encrypted data key.
- Key access: when a decryption operation is needed, Redwood will call your KMS using the key ARN; the KMS performs the decryption. If you use an HSM-backed key in your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with AWS CloudHSM backing), the key material remains in the HSM.

2) HSM / Redwood Private:
- For HSM-level assurance we support two patterns: 
  a) Hosted + CMEK backed by cloud-KMS with HSM: you provision an HSM-backed key in your AWS/GCP/Azure KMS and provide the ARN to Redwood.
  b) Private deployment: Redwood Private can be deployed in your VPC and connect to an on-prem or customer-managed HSM via a KMS bridge; in that model, key operations never leave your environment.

3) Logs & PII:
- Audit logs: we provide request-level audit logs that include metadata (timestamp, request id, model, token counts, key-id used).
- Payloads: sensitive input/output are redacted by default from Redwood-managed logs. We offer an option to disable storing payloads in Redwood-managed storage altogether; instead, logs (including any payloads you opt to keep) can be delivered to your S3/GCS endpoint encrypted with your CMEK.

4) Retention & purge:
- We expose retention windows per-customer and an API endpoint for data deletion. When you call the purge API we will remove tenant data from primary storage and from snapshots/backups within the SLA we agree to in the contract (typical SLA is 30 days for full backup purge; can be negotiated for stricter terms).
